# Sigil Engineering

> The discipline of recovering stable conceptual structures from narratives, precisely enough that people and AI agents can inhabit them. This site publishes the method's own specification — the spec from which the Sigil editor was projected.

## Machine-readable spec

The full specification is available as JSON:

- URL: https://sigilengineering.com/sigil-spec.json
- Format: a JSON tree of sigils. Each node has `name`, `language` (markdown narrative), `affordances` (list of `{name, content}`), `invariants` (list of `{name, content}`), and `children` (nested sigils).

## Vocabulary

A sigil is a bounded region of language: a lexical scope with affordances (what can be done there) and invariants (what must stay true there). Sigils nest; the root sigil is the application itself. In the narratives, `@name` references a sigil, `#name` an affordance, `!name` an invariant — each resolving through ancestor scopes, like lexical scoping.

## How to use

Load /sigil-spec.json and walk the tree. Each sigil's `language` is written in the vocabulary of its children. Affordances are the feature list; invariants are the test suite; the language narrative is the acceptance test.
